reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern exhibits a robust quasi-periodic structure with a fundamental period of ~98 points, as confirmed by the estimated period and window_cycles scaling (1P, 3P, 3P, 5P). Each cycle contains one dominant sharp positive spike (peak amplitude 3–5 robust std units), typically preceded by a gradual rise and followed by a rapid decay to near-baseline or slightly negative values. Baseline levels fluctuate mildly around zero (median within ±0.16), with no strong monotonic trend across candidates—slope_per_point values are near-zero (±0.012), indicating local stationarity despite global difference-stationarity. Peaks are asymmetric: steep ascent (~5–10 points) and sharper descent (~3–7 points), often with minor pre-peak shoulders or post-peak undershoots. Troughs are shallow and broad, rarely exceeding −1.0, and often cluster near zero. Noise is low-to-moderate: roughness ~0.11–0.13, curvature ~0.25–0.37, suggesting smooth but non-sinusoidal oscillations. Amplitude_90 varies (3.28–5.03) due to window length and local scaling, but peak height distribution is consistent: most spikes reach 3–4.5 units, with occasional outliers up to ~5.2. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates show full cycles without abrupt cutoffs. Acceptable variation includes: (1) slight baseline drift over longer windows (e.g., ref 3 shows mild upward drift early), (2) minor differences in trough depth and inter-spike spacing (±5–10 points), and (3) presence/absence of small secondary bumps near peaks. Crucially, the spike morphology—sharp, isolated, unimodal positive excursions—is highly conserved across all four candidates.

Baseline drifts subtly upward (slope +0.0023), but remains centered near 0.16. One flat segment (951–966) may indicate sensor saturation or artifact, but does not disrupt periodicity.

Another 3-cycle excerpt (294 pts); spikes at ~1750, 1850, 1950 are sharper and taller than ref 1, with stronger asymmetry (steeper descent). Baseline near −0.06, stable. Minor troughs dip below −1.0 more frequently. No flat segments; noise slightly higher (mad 0.667 vs 0.691), but morphology aligns closely with ref 1 and 3.

Long 5-cycle excerpt (490 pts); displays five spikes with increasing amplitude toward the end (last spike ~5.2). Baseline drifts slightly downward early (slope −0.001), then stabilizes. Inter-spike intervals vary modestly (90–105 pts), but spike shape remains consistent. Higher amplitude_90 reflects cumulative range over longer window, not local anomaly. Most comprehensive view of normal variability.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 3 for queries with ≥4 cycles or ambiguous baseline trends—it provides the most robust morphological consensus. Use reference 0 for short query windows (<150 pts) where single-spike fidelity matters. Reference 2 is best for queries with sharp, high-amplitude spikes and deeper troughs; reference 1 is acceptable but treat its flat segment as a potential outlier—avoid using it when query shows no plateau. When query spike width or asymmetry deviates significantly from refs 0/2/3 (e.g., broad symmetric humps), suspect anomaly regardless of amplitude.
uncertainties: Whether the flat segment in ref 1 is sensor artifact or legitimate normal behavior—insufficient evidence to confirm
Exact tolerance for inter-spike interval deviation (±10 pts observed; unknown if >15 pts is anomalous)
Whether mild amplitude growth over 5 cycles (ref 3) is systematic or stochastic—requires more long-window references
